title: Sensitization is common in biological pathway models but rare in random networks

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Sensitization is common in biological pathway models but rare in random networks

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: Sensitization (a progressive 1.5-fold increase in response over repeated stimulations) was found in 27 of the 35 BioModels pathway models, whereas very few random gene-circuit models showed it (under 10% of pairings per model), suggesting the feature may be unique to biology or require more complex random models.

fields.label: Work
fields.value: Learning in Transcriptional Network Models: Computational Discovery of Pathway-Level Memory and Effective Interventions

fields.label: Chapter
fields.value: Biswas S 2022, Learning in Transcriptional Network Models: Computational Discovery of Pathway-Level Memory and Effective Interventions › 2. Results › 2.8. Making and Breaking Sensitization

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: Interestingly, very few of the random models had UCS-R relations that generated sensitization (<10% of UCS-R pairings per model), indicating that this feature may be unique to biology, or that more complex random models would be needed to find such behavior (Figure 10 and Figures S17–S19).

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: Biswas S, Clawson W, Levin M, “Learning in Transcriptional Network Models: Computational Discovery of Pathway-Level Memory and Effective Interventions”, International journal of molecular sciences (2022), doi:10.3390/ijms24010285; section “2. Results › 2.8. Making and Breaking Sensitization”. Scope: 35 BioModels pathway models versus 500 random gene-circuit models

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on levin-2022-grn-learning-17: partially-resolvable, resolvability 0.84

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: The reported prevalence contrast is reproducible. The stronger suggestion of biological uniqueness is not resolved by one random-network family.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Recompute sensitization under the 1.5-fold criterion in all biological and random models and compare prevalence distributions. The numerical difference is testable, while uniqueness to biology requires broader null ensembles and biological systems.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Simulation sensitization is a proxy for biological sensitization.

The random ensemble may be too simple to support comparable dynamics.

data existence: 0.88

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: The 1.5-fold rule and both arms of the comparison can be rerun from public code and BioModels. The biological count is a direct check. The inference that sensitization is unique to biology, or requires more complex random models, is not identified by this null, so the claim is only partly resolved by the rerun.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Score a pair as sensitizing when the response rises at least 1.5-fold across six lengthening stimulations, and compare the fraction of biological models that have any such pair with the per-model pair rate in the random circuits. Twenty-seven of 35 biological models, against under 10 percent of random pairings, would reproduce the counts; a high random rate would refute uniqueness.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
The random null uses a different ODE family, so rarity there does not show the behaviour is unique to biology.

The paper itself allows that more complex random models might show sensitization.
